v.why: With edge 1->3 absent, a direct conv path 0->3 restores much more of the output node's input (exp 3 vs 1-2).
Removing edge 0->3 when edge 1->3 is also absent starves the output node and can disconnect the cell (exp 72, 74).
Deleting edge 1->3 when edge 2->3 is absent leaves the output with too few or no incoming paths (exp 43, 44).
Adding a conv into the output matters much more when edge 0->3 is missing (exp 17).
In parameter-free skip-dominated cells, another skip on 0->3 short-circuits learning, while conv-heavy cells benefit from the residual (exp 38 vs 31-34).
Adding a first trainable conv to a skip-dominated cell gives very large gains compared with conv-rich parents (exp 28-29 vs 21-27).
A conv on edge 2->3 rescues collapsed parameter-free cells but adds little to conv-rich ones (exp 85 vs 11-20).
Replacing the conv on 0->2 is nearly harmless when other convs remain, but devastating when it is the only conv (exp 51-60 vs 54, 59).
An extra conv on 1->2 is redundant when edge 0->1 is already a 3x3 conv, but helpful in skip or 1x1 cells (exp 61-67 vs 68-69).
Adding a residual where no 0->3 path existed helps more than swapping out an existing conv or pool on that edge (exp 31-34, 39-40 vs 36-37).

The hypotheses below come from reading the 100 experiments by eye. I did not run any statistics. Most follow one structural pattern: an edit's effect is largest when the parent is close to a degenerate cell.

**Main patterns in the data**
- **Output node starved:** Node 3 is fed only by edges 3, 4 and 5. If the parent has most of those set to `none`, adding a conv to the output is worth a lot (up to about +78 points on C10, experiments 3, 17 and 93). Removing an output edge is correspondingly catastrophic (experiments 44 and 72).
- **Parameter-free parents:** Cells made only of `skip_connect` or `avg_pool_3x3` collapse. In those parents, adding any `nor_conv_3x3` gives a gain of +40 points or more (experiments 29, 30, 85 and 89). Removing the single conv, or adding another parameter-free op, hurts badly (experiments 35, 38, 54 and 59).
- **Conv-rich parents:** In these the same edits mostly change accuracy by only about ±2 points.
